questions.question: Can gasoline be brought onto a bus?

options.text: Yes, it can be brought onto a bus.
No, it can never be brought onto a bus.
Yes, it can be stored in the passenger area during long trips.
Yes, if it is stored in glass containers.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it can never be brought onto a bus.
questions.explanation: Gasoline and other hazardous items like car batteries are not allowed on buses. This protects drivers and passengers from danger.

questions.question: What should happen if a bus breaks down while carrying passengers?

options.text: Another bus should push the disabled bus to its final destination.
The bus should be towed to the final destination with passengers still on board.
The bus should be towed to the nearest safe location so passengers can get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus should be towed to the nearest safe location so passengers can get off.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not stay on a bus while it is being towed or pushed, unless it is unsafe for them to leave. In that case, the bus should be towed to the nearest safe spot where passengers can exit.

questions.question: How can poisonous fumes enter a truck cab?

options.text: From using the wrong type of fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: From a broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly when a tire fails. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Once it is going slowly, brake gently and pull off the road. Then check your tires.

questions.question: Why should you accelerate slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always the right choice.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
To stay behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery roads. Using too much power can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When approaching a drawbridge with a green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping.
You must wait for the light to turn yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through without stopping.
questions.explanation: A green light at a drawbridge means you do not need to stop. However, always slow down before crossing to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?

options.text: A B or C fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: A B or C fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: Use B or C type fire extinguishers on electrical fires. Never use water on an electrical fire because it can cause electric shock.

questions.question: During backing exercises (not the straight line exercise), how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can look one time. For other exercises, you can look two times.

questions.question: Are the heights posted at bridges always accurate?
questions.correctAnswerText: No, they can be incorrect.
questions.explanation: Never assume that posted bridge heights are correct. Road conditions can change, such as repaving or snow buildup, which affects clearance.

questions.question: When making a left turn with two turn lanes available, why should you use the rightmost lane?

options.text: You can better see other vehicles turning on your left instead of your right.
Your vehicle can turn more quickly.
Other vehicles will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can better see other vehicles turning on your left instead of your right.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles swing right to turn left. Starting in the rightmost lane puts other turning traffic on your left where you can see it better. This helps you avoid collisions with other turning vehicles.

questions.question: After changing a tire, a driver should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check that the tire is wearing evenly.
Check that the tire air pressure is correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After driving with a new tire, stop soon to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When checking tires, which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: Front tires with at least 4/32 inch of tread in the grooves
Mixing radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tires with at least 4/32 inch of tread in the grooves
questions.explanation: Check that air pressure is correct. Check that front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Never mix radial and bias-ply tires on the same vehicle.

questions.question: To stay alert while driving, you should:

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Drive with a second person who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with a second person who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Sharing driving duties with another driver reduces fatigue. Avoid heavy foods and keep the cab cool to stay alert.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is clear ice on the road surface. The road may look wet but is actually icy. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ makes steering difficult.
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. More play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Countersteer.
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake to let the wheels roll. Steer toward where you want to go, then countersteer to prevent the vehicle from skidding the other way.

questions.question: Always do a pre-trip inspection in the same order because:

options.text: You are less likely to forget something.
You will finish the inspection faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order each time helps you remember all the steps. You will be less likely to skip anything when following a set checklist.

questions.question: Most bus accidents happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most bus accidents happen at intersections. Use caution at all intersections, even those with signs or signals.

questions.question: When speeding up on a slippery surface like a wet road, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.question: The minimum tread depth for rear tires is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Rear tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on a vehicle should be the same size.
